topics.mining: Bedrock cannot be broken or collected through ordinary Survival mining, even with Silk Touch.
topics.location: Bedrock forms the bottom boundary of the Overworld and the floor and ceiling boundaries of the Nether. It also appears in End portal and gateway structures.
topics.operation: Bedrock is an unbreakable world boundary during normal Survival play. It is not a mineable ore or a craftable building resource.

topics.mining: Trying to mine a dragon egg normally makes it teleport. A piston can push it into item form, or let it fall onto a suitable non-full block such as a torch to collect it.
topics.location: Look at the End exit portal after defeating the Ender Dragon.
topics.operation: The dragon egg is a trophy. It does not hatch into a baby dragon or respawn the Ender Dragon by itself.

topics.mining: This pumpkin block drops itself by hand or with any tool; an axe is fastest.
topics.location: Use shears on a pumpkin to carve it.
topics.operation: Use a carved pumpkin as headwear or as the final block when constructing a suitable golem.

topics.mining: This pumpkin block drops itself by hand or with any tool; an axe is fastest.
topics.location: Craft a jack o lantern from a carved pumpkin and a torch.
topics.operation: A jack o lantern gives steady light. It does not need fuel or redstone power.

topics.mining: Golden dandelions drop themselves by hand or with any tool.
topics.location: Craft a golden dandelion from a dandelion and 8 gold nuggets.
topics.operation: Use a golden dandelion on a supported baby mob to pause its growth; use it again to resume growth. It is not a normal breeding food.

topics.mining: Leaf litter drops itself by hand or with any tool. The number dropped matches the pieces placed in that block space.
topics.location: Find leaf litter beneath trees in suitable forest biomes, or obtain it through its supported smelting recipes.
topics.operation: Place multiple pieces in a block space as decorative ground cover. Leaf litter can also be used as fuel.

topics.mining: Use shears or a Silk Touch tool to collect dry grass. Otherwise it drops nothing.
topics.location: Look in deserts and badlands.
topics.growth: Dry grass is desert vegetation. Bone meal can grow or spread its appropriate short and tall forms; it does not produce wheat seeds like ordinary grass.

topics.mining: Use shears or a Silk Touch tool to collect dry grass. Otherwise it drops nothing.
topics.location: Look in deserts and badlands.
topics.growth: Dry grass is desert vegetation. Bone meal can grow or spread its appropriate short and tall forms; it does not produce wheat seeds like ordinary grass.

topics.mining: This plant drops itself when broken by hand or with any tool.
topics.location: Look for it in on fallen poplar logs in dappled forests.
topics.operation: Use it as decorative vegetation on a compatible supporting surface.

topics.mining: This plant drops itself when broken by hand or with any tool.
topics.location: Look for it in dappled forests.
topics.operation: Use it as decorative vegetation on a compatible supporting surface.

topics.mining: An unused straw bed drops itself when broken; a hoe is fastest. After sleeping in it, the bed is consumed instead.
topics.location: Craft straw beds from hay bales or find them in abandoned camps.
topics.operation: A straw bed is a single-use sleeping place. It does not reset your respawn point like an ordinary bed.
topics.danger: Do not try to sleep in a straw bed in the Nether or the End; beds explode there.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect potent sulfur. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing.
topics.location: Find potent sulfur in sulfur pools in sulfur caves and sulfur springs.
topics.operation: Potent sulfur under suitable water can produce noxious gas at the surface. It is not merely decorative ordinary sulfur.
topics.danger: Noxious gas above a suitable potent-sulfur water setup can cause nausea. Keep clear of the gas when exploring sulfur pools.

topics.mining: Sulfur spikes drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. A thrown trident can break them.
topics.location: Find spikes in sulfur caves and around sulfur springs.
topics.operation: Use sulfur spikes for cave decoration or compatible sulfur recipes. Removing a supporting formation can make parts fall.

topics.mining: Use a bucket on a source block to collect this fluid. Ordinary mining and Silk Touch do not produce a placeable fluid block item.
topics.location: Water occurs in rivers, lakes, oceans and aquifers in the Overworld.
topics.operation: Use water for irrigation, travel, extinguishing fire and water-based mechanisms. Water placed normally in the Nether evaporates.

topics.mining: Use a bucket on a source block to collect this fluid. Ordinary mining and Silk Touch do not produce a placeable fluid block item.
topics.location: Find lava underground in the Overworld and in large seas and pockets in the Nether.
topics.operation: Lava is a dangerous fluid that burns many entities and dropped items. Lava buckets can be used as furnace fuel.

topics.mining: Bubble columns are not collectible blocks. Collect their water with a bucket or change the base block to remove the effect.
topics.location: Place soul sand or magma beneath a column of water source blocks.
topics.operation: Soul sand creates upward bubbles; magma creates downward bubbles. Flowing water needs to become source blocks before the full column works.

topics.mining: Fire cannot be collected by mining or Silk Touch. Extinguish it rather than trying to pick it up.
topics.location: Light suitable surfaces with an ignition source.
topics.danger: Touching fire can hurt and ignite vulnerable entities. Keep flammable builds and dropped items away from it.

topics.mining: Fire cannot be collected by mining or Silk Touch. Extinguish it rather than trying to pick it up.
topics.location: Ignite soul sand or soul soil to make soul fire.
topics.danger: Touching fire can hurt and ignite vulnerable entities. Keep flammable builds and dropped items away from it.

topics.mining: Heads and skulls drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Place heads for decoration or wear compatible heads. Some heads have special uses, such as Wither skeleton skulls for Wither construction and heads above note blocks for mob sounds.

topics.mining: This portal block cannot be collected through normal Survival mining, even with Silk Touch.
topics.operation: A Nether portal is created by lighting a valid obsidian frame. Breaking the portal blocks does not give a collectible portal item.
topics.location: Build an appropriate obsidian frame to form a Nether portal.

topics.mining: This portal block cannot be collected through normal Survival mining, even with Silk Touch.
topics.operation: An End portal forms when a valid frame is completed with eyes of ender. Portal blocks are not collectible building blocks in ordinary Survival.
topics.location: Find End portal structures in strongholds.

topics.mining: This portal block cannot be collected through normal Survival mining, even with Silk Touch.
topics.operation: End portal frames occur in strongholds and cannot be mined or crafted in ordinary Survival. Complete the frame with eyes of ender to activate the portal.
topics.location: Find End portal structures in strongholds.

topics.mining: Element blocks drop themselves instantly when broken.
topics.location: Elements belong to the Education chemistry features. Use an element constructor in a world with those features available; they are not ordinary Survival ores.
topics.operation: Use elements as inputs for supported chemistry compounds and experiments. The proton, neutron and electron counts define the element or isotope.

topics.mining: Hardened glass drops itself even when broken by hand. Silk Touch is unnecessary; it behaves differently from ordinary glass.
topics.location: Hardened glass is an Education chemistry material made from glass and appropriate compounds in a world supporting those features.
topics.operation: Use hardened glass as a tougher transparent building material. It is not ordinary stained glass.

topics.location: Invisible light blocks are creator tools obtained through commands or compatible Creative tools, not normal Survival crafting.
topics.operation: Light blocks add invisible lighting at a selected light level. They are intended for map building rather than ordinary Survival resource gathering.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Allow blocks permit building and breaking above them under the applicable Education/adventure rules.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Deny blocks prevent building and breaking above them under the applicable Education/adventure rules.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Border blocks create a special impassable world boundary under the applicable Education rules.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Barrier blocks are invisible collision blocks used by map makers.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Structure void preserves existing space when using structure tools; it is not an ordinary solid building block.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Jigsaw blocks help creators assemble generated structure pieces.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Structure blocks save and load structures for world-building workflows.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: The camera block belongs to specialized Education features; it is not a normal Survival recipe.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Use this Education chemistry station to combine appropriate elements into compounds.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Use this Education chemistry station to choose protons, neutrons and electrons to construct elements.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Use this Education chemistry station for supported compound experiments.

topics.location: This is a specialized creator or Education block. It is not obtained by ordinary Survival crafting or mining.
topics.operation: Use this Education chemistry station to break supported materials into element outputs.

topics.location: Command blocks are creator tools obtained with authorized commands and Creative access, not ordinary Survival crafting.
topics.operation: Command blocks run configured commands when their conditions are met. Impulse, repeating and chain forms are different command execution modes.

topics.location: A piston head appears as part of an extended piston; it is not an independently craftable block.
topics.operation: Operate the piston base with redstone. The head is part of that mechanism, not a separate item you need to collect.

topics.location: Air is empty world space, not a collectible Survival resource.
topics.operation: Air blocks provide empty space for movement, placement and other world mechanics.

topics.location: This placeholder is not an ordinary Survival resource or recipe output.
topics.operation: An unknown block is a placeholder for content the game cannot interpret. Check the world or add-on compatibility rather than treating it as a resource.

topics.location: Colored torches are Education chemistry items, made using compatible torch and compound recipes.
topics.operation: Colored torches provide light with their distinct appearance. They are not redstone torches.

topics.location: Underwater torches belong to the Education chemistry features.
topics.operation: Unlike an ordinary torch, an underwater torch can provide light underwater in worlds supporting the chemistry features.

topics.location: Underwater TNT is an Education chemistry explosive, not an ordinary TNT variant obtained by mining.
topics.danger: Underwater TNT can cause destructive explosions underwater. Keep players and valued builds away from a primed explosive.

topics.location: Heat blocks belong to Education chemistry features.
topics.operation: A heat block can melt nearby ice and snow without emitting light in supported Education worlds.
